selection_rationale: Candidate cnd-2026-netops-gvr-eval-01 directly targets the highest-priority unresolved question (end-to-end reliability of generate→verify→repair pipelines), is experimentally falsifiable, feasible within available resources, and received a 'pass' verdict from the critic review. It yields clear paired outcomes for rigorous statistical testing and aligns closely with CNSM Agentic-AI-for-NetOps relevance.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier coverage limits vs. semantic/operational properties that are hard to encode in the verifier (will affect attribution of residual failures).
Emulator fidelity / vendor-specific CLI and rollback semantics may diverge from production behavior and bias safety estimates.
Single-hosted-model evaluation limits external validity (model heterogeneity and non-determinism may affect repeatability/generalizability).
Model-provider non-determinism and API-side changes (versions, rate limits) could inflate outcome variance relative to preregistered assumptions.
Potential need to redact or otherwise responsibly disclose sensitive artefacts if certain repair/attack templates emerge during failure analysis.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Add explicit verifier-coverage tests (oracle/unit tasks) that enumerate which property-classes the verifier fully supports and document verifier limitations per property class.
Document emulator fidelity limits and scope; include at least one vendor-like behavioral test or clearly state out-of-scope vendor semantics (rollback/CLI differences) in the preregistration.

Prespecify and freeze retry policy, exact random seeds, API/model version identifiers, logging/recording of nondeterministic runs, and how retries for infrastructure failures differ from scientific retries.

Either include a small multi-model robustness check (e.g., one additional hosted or local smaller model) or provide a preregistered justification for a single-model design and specify how generalizability will be qualified in threats-to-validity.
